outcomes: A feature owns migration sources while one runner owns execution for each migration kind
Applying the same registered set repeatedly is ordered and idempotent
An operator detects hash drift and missing registered or stored migrations before release
A failed migration cannot be reported as successfully applied
nonGoals: Making all migration kinds or datasources one distributed atomic transaction
Inferring rollback SQL when a migration author did not provide it
Starting runtime listeners as part of migration execution
Specifying SQL execution atomicity, drift, or reversibility, which go/sql-migration-execution owns

requirements.text: Contributed kinds execute in lexicographic order and the registry aggregates per-kind results in that same order; per-kind execution order is the owning runner's, specified by go/sql-migration-execution.
Exactly one runner may own a kind and explicit apply, rollback, status, and verify fail before execution when contributed sources have no runner.
